title: The Vale of Ash
intro: The barrow on the hill has opened, and a gray blight creeps down the vale. Crops fail. Roads empty. The village of Last Light holds on at the wood's edge. Someone must go up to the barrow and end this. Two paths lead there, each enough on its own: the three old verses — one in the drowned shrine, one atop the old watchtower, one cut into the barrow's own walls — or the king's own crown, said to lie sealed in the village elder's coffer. Choose one — you need not chase both, and the two roads end the tale differently. You walked in at dusk.

warden.name: Warden
warden.desc: strong, steady, hard to kill — verses go slow without a scholar's eye, but steel can settle this without them

scout.name: Scout
scout.desc: quick and quiet; finds hidden ways — a light touch can read a verse or spring a lock others can't

scholar.name: Scholar
scholar.desc: best suited to the verse path — reads the old tongue, recalls each verse outright, no check or puzzle needed — no tougher in a fight than the rest

envoy.name: Envoy
envoy.desc: best suited to the crown path — words open doors that iron cannot, a silver tongue may win it quicker than any verse

descs: Ash trees close in, gray on gray.

spots.name: The Split Oak
spots.desc: An oak split clean by old lightning right at the wood's edge. The village lanterns still show through the gap behind you. East and a little north, past the trunks, the old watchtower breaks the skyline, and past it the drowned shrine shows as a dull gleam of still water among the trees.
spots.brief: The split oak. The way out — village lanterns show south, behind you.

actions.label: get your bearings
fx: You picture the wood as it lies: a loose square of trails around this oak. The village lanterns stay south, behind you. The tower and the drowned shrine lie east, the barrow trail runs north, and a hunter's camp lies west. Lost, just backtrack the way you came.

spots.name: Broken Bridge
spots.desc: A footbridge, half fallen into a dry streambed. The far rail is gone. Woodsmoke drifts from the north; the village lanterns show through the trees east.
spots.brief: The broken bridge. Woodsmoke drifts north; the Split Oak, and the way to the village, lies east.

actions.label: get your bearings
fx: You picture the wood as it lies: a loose square of trails, not a straight one — only the Split Oak, where lantern light shows through a gap in the branches, leads back to the village. The barrow trail lies north, the drowned shrine and the old watchtower east, the hunter's camp west. Lost, just backtrack the way you came — that always works.

spots.desc: A ring of blackened stone. Someone camped here, and not recently. The village lies west, the barrow trail runs north, and the trail continues east past a marker stake.
spots.brief: The charcoal ring. The village lies west, via the Split Oak; the barrow trail runs north; the trail continues east.

spots.brief: Tower shadow. The watchtower's a few steps east. Village only south, via the Split Oak.

spots.brief: Herb hollow, good for wounds. The barrow trail lies west; the wood continues south and east.

spots.name: Crow Perch
spots.desc: A blasted, leafless tree stands alone, hung with black feathers instead of leaves. Bare sky north and east — nothing that way. The barrow trail lies west, past the thinning trees; the watchtower's shadow falls south.
spots.brief: Crow perch. Nothing north or east but bare sky. The barrow trail lies west; the watchtower's shadow falls south.

gate.name: Village Gate
gate.desc: The last gate before the wood. Lanterns burn all day here now. Two roads lead to the barrow ahead, either enough alone: the old verses, hidden in the wood and the barrow's own walls, or the king's crown, locked in the village elder's coffer. The square lies south, where the reeve's notice board holds the fuller account, including why the reeve and the gray priest don't agree on the barrow. The Ashwood waits north, where trails split off toward the drowned shrine and the old watchtower.

actions.label: get your bearings
fx: The wood runs north from here — go north to enter it. Straight through takes you to the barrow trail if that's your road. But word in the square is it hides more: once inside, a drowned shrine and an old watchtower lie east, a hunter's camp west — get your bearings again once you're among the trees, it'll walk you the rest of the way.

actions.label: follow the trail north to the barrow
head into the ashwood — the drowned shrine and old watchtower lie east

follow the trail east to the old watchtower

square.name: Last Light Square
square.desc: Packed earth and a dry well. The reeve stands watch by a notice board — the short of it, verses or crown, either alone ends this; read the board for the rest. Inn west, forge east, chapel south.

actions.label: read the notice board
fx: Notice board: the dead king in the barrow won't rest. Either the old verses or his crown can settle him alone — no need to chase both. The reeve wants the barrow sealed shut for good after; the gray priest, in the chapel south past the well, wants it opened instead — he remembers the old king's grief and thinks the dead deserve better than a stone lid.

actions.label: read the notice board again
fx: More, in a finer hand: one path is the old verses. Three lie in the drowned shrine, the old watchtower — through the gate, then east into the ash wood (get your bearings once you're among the trees) — and the barrow's own walls. Speak all three together at the throne.

actions.label: read the notice board again
fx: Another hand added: or seek the king's crown. The elder's locked coffer holds it, taken from him long ago — the reason his rest won't come. Hear his grief at the throne first, then press the elder for it.

actions.label: read the notice board again
fx: A last line, added later: either path ends it alone, though the two together leave nothing unresolved. Mind — the verses read quick only for a scholar's eye; anyone else puzzles them out slow, deep in the wood, three sites over — or asks the wandering scholar warming their hands at the inn west for the trick of it. The crown is the steadier road if that's not your gift — one lock in the vault for the seal, then the elder to convince.

actions.label: follow the trail north to the barrow
follow the trail east to the drowned shrine
follow the trail east to the old watchtower
follow the trail west to the hunter's camp
take stock of the verses
fx: None of the three verses are yours yet.

inn.name: The Last Light Inn
inn.desc: A low fire, empty tables, and an innkeep glad of any face. The square lies east.

actions.label: rest by the fire
fx: You sleep without dreams and wake steadier.

forge.name: The Forge
forge.desc: Coals banked low. The smith works with the door open, watching the road. Iron and old smoke hang in the air. The square lies west.

chapel.name: Gray Chapel
chapel.desc: A small stone chapel. Candles against the dark. The priest wears ash on both hands. Wax and damp stone smell like the inside of a well. A door east leads to the elder's house.

elder_house.name: Elder's House
elder_house.desc: Ledgers, dust, and an iron coffer on the mantel, locked over some old claim. The elder receives you without a smile. The shutters are closed against the wood. The chapel lies west.

hunters_camp.name: Hunter's Camp
hunters_camp.desc: A lean-to and a smoke rack at the wood's west edge. The hunter watches the trees, not you.

actions.label: follow the trail south back to the village gate

drowned_chapel.name: Drowned Shrine
drowned_chapel.desc: Half a chapel, sunk to its windows in black water. A stone psalter stands above the waterline, its verses cut for a king who cannot rest. The trail south leads back to the village gate.

actions.label: follow the trail south back to the village gate
recall the water verse (scholar)
fx: The water verse comes back to you, line by line. Water Verse: obtained.

actions.label: trace the water verse by touch (scout)
fx: Quiet fingers trace the worn grooves, reading the shape of the words by feel. Water Verse: obtained.

The grooves give up nothing yet. Slow going without a scholar's eye — not shut to one; a defter touch (grace) reads it faster, and nothing is lost by trying again. Or leave it: the elder's crown reaches the same end without a verse.

actions.label: work out the water verse
fx: The worn lines give up their meaning. Water Verse: obtained.

The water has taken too much. Slow going without a scholar's eye — not shut to one; a sharper mind (wits) reads it faster, the wandering scholar at the inn may lend you one, and nothing is lost by trying again. Or leave it: the elder's crown reaches the same end without a verse.

watchtower.name: Old Watchtower
watchtower.desc: An old watchtower, stairs still sound. Wind carvings ring the bell room at the top, words meant for the same king's ear. The trail south leads back to the village gate.

actions.label: follow the trail south back to the village gate
recall the wind verse (scholar)
fx: The wind verse comes back to you, whole. Wind Verse: obtained.

actions.label: work out the wind carvings
fx: The carvings give up their meaning. Wind Verse: obtained.

The lines blur. Slow going without a scholar's eye — not shut to one; a sharper mind (wits) reads it faster, the wandering scholar at the inn may lend you one, and nothing is lost by trying again. Or leave it: the elder's crown reaches the same end without a verse.

barrow_field.name: Barrow Field
barrow_field.desc: A bare hill and two stone doors set into it, facing north. The grass here is white, not gray. The trail south leads back to the village gate.

north.lockedMsg: The stone doors are shut fast. Force might open them, ask the gray priest for a blessing, or search the hillside — roots and old rain may have hollowed a way in somewhere else.
north.hint: force the doors, get the priest's blessing, or search the hillside

onEnterOnce: So this is where the gray begins.

actions.label: get your bearings
fx: From the hilltop you can see it plain: the village lies south down the trail, and past the wood to the east stand the drowned shrine and the old watchtower. Quickest way there is back down to the gate, then north into the wood and east from there — no need to cut cross-country from here.

actions.label: follow the trail south back to the village gate
force the doors
fx: Stone grinds on stone. The doors open.
The doors do not move. Try again, ask the gray priest for a blessing, or search the hillside for another way in.

actions.label: force the doors
fx: Stone grinds on stone. The doors open.
The doors do not move. The priest won't help now, sworn as you are — brace and try again, or search the hillside for another way in.

actions.label: force the doors (warden)
fx: One good shoulder is all it takes. Stone grinds on stone and gives way at once — steel and muscle settle it without a verse or a blessing. The doors open.

actions.label: search for the keeper's crack (scout)
fx: A narrow gap behind the ivy — no need for the priest's blessing after all. You work it wider and slip through.
Nothing yet. The hill keeps its secrets — force or a blessing could still open the doors outright.

actions.label: search the hillside for a hidden passage
fx: Roots and old rain have hollowed a gap beneath a fallen lintel stone. You squeeze through into the dark below.
The hillside holds its shape. Nothing gives way yet — force or a blessing could still open the doors outright.

antechamber.name: Barrow Antechamber
antechamber.desc: Cut stone, older than the village. Shelf niches stand empty. A passage north leads deeper into the barrow — the way on, toward the throne. A heavy door stands east, iron-strapped like a vault holding some locked prize. A passage down breathes cold air up from a crypt of low vaults, old gear worth taking, and whatever still guards it. Neither lies on the way through, but skip them and you skip only plunder, not progress.
onEnterOnce: These niches once held tokens for the dead. Go before the king with nothing to offer him — no verse, no crown — and he may just take you instead.

vault.name: Vault
vault.desc: A side chamber the wight never had to guard — the old king trusted iron more than claws. A strongbox sits under years of dust, its lock long rusted. The antechamber lies west.
onEnterOnce: Whatever this held, no one has touched it in a long time.

actions.label: force the strongbox
fx: The rusted lock snaps at last. Inside: a seal of office, wrapped around a scrap of the king's own writing.
The lock holds, this time. Rusted iron, not sealed magic — keep at it and it will give.

actions.label: pick the strongbox's lock (scout)
fx: The old pins give way, one by one. Inside: a seal of office, wrapped around a scrap of the king's own writing.
Not yet, but the pins are turning. Keep working the lock and it will open.

actions.label: read the king's writing
fx: "Forty years I kept faith. It was my own blood who lifted the crown from my sleeping brow and called it inheritance. I do not want the vale to suffer for his theft. I only wanted to be believed."

hall_of_verses.name: Hall of Verses
hall_of_verses.desc: Every wall is cut with lines of old writing — the same king's verses, meant to be spoken over him. Some of it almost reads itself. The antechamber lies south; a stair climbs up to the throne.

up.lockedMsg: There is a stair here somewhere. The walls say where.
up.hint: read the stone verse on these walls first

actions.label: study the stone walls (scholar)
fx: The stone verse reads itself to you: a stair is cut into the wall right here, leading up. Stone Verse: obtained.

actions.label: work out the stone verse
fx: The verse comes clear: a stair is cut into the wall right here, leading up. Stone Verse: obtained.

The old letters swim. Slow going without a scholar's eye — not shut to one; a sharper mind (wits) reads it faster, the wandering scholar at the inn may lend you one, and nothing is lost by trying again. Or leave it: the crypt north of the antechamber reaches the throne without this verse, if the crown is your road.

crypt.name: Crypt
crypt.desc: Low vaults and stone boxes. A mail shirt is draped over one, there for the taking. Something stands between you and the north passage. Old halls like this rarely have only one door.

north.lockedMsg: The wight bars the way north.
north.hint: defeat or slip past the wight first

actions.label: slip past the wight (scout)
fx: You keep to the shadow and slip by.
Claws rake you as you dart back. Quiet hands can try again — or stand and fight it here.

throne.name: Throne of the Barrow
throne.desc: The Hollow King sits on a stone seat. Where a crown should be, there is nothing. The air is very still. A passage south leads to the crypt; a stair down returns to the hall of verses.
onEnterOnce: So this is where it ends. Whatever you choose here decides how. Speak the verses if you carry them, or bring back his crown — either lets him rest. Kneel to him empty-handed and you take up his crown for your own — and linger here in his place, with no dawn to come for you.

actions.label: leave the barrow and head back to the village gate
speak the three verses at the throne, leaving the barrow open
fx: You speak the three verses, binding him fast to his rest. The grief that spilled out as blight goes still with him, and the gray lifts from the vale by morning. The barrow doors stand open behind you — you made the reeve no promise to shut them. Within the week moss greens the well-stones and the market fills again, though half the vale still glances at the barrow mouth on their way past.

actions.label: speak the three verses at the throne, sealing the barrow after, as you promised the reeve
fx: You speak the three verses, binding him fast to his rest. The grief that spilled out as blight goes still with him, and the gray lifts from the vale by morning. True to your word, the barrow doors seal shut behind you for good. Within the week moss greens the well-stones and the market fills again — no one glances at the barrow mouth anymore, since there is nothing left to see.

actions.label: the stone verse is still unspoken
fx: It waits down these stairs, cut into the Hall of Verses.

actions.label: the water verse is still unspoken
fx: It waits in the drowned shrine, east of the wood — you'd need to leave the barrow and go back through the gate to reach it.

actions.label: the wind verse is still unspoken
fx: It waits atop the old watchtower — you'd need to leave the barrow and go back through the gate to reach it.

actions.label: return the crown, leaving the barrow open
fx: You set the crown in his hands. He stands, bows once, and lies down at last. The gray goes out of the trees like a tide. The barrow doors stand open behind you — you made the reeve no promise to shut them. Grass pushes up through the ash by the next full moon, and the reeve posts a notice thanking whoever settled the old king's account, name withheld.

actions.label: return the crown, sealing the barrow after, as you promised the reeve
fx: You set the crown in his hands. He stands, bows once, and lies down at last. The gray goes out of the trees like a tide. True to your word, the barrow doors seal shut behind you for good. Grass pushes up through the ash by the next full moon, and the reeve posts a notice thanking whoever settled the old king's account, name withheld.

actions.label: return the crown and speak the three verses, leaving the barrow open
fx: You set the crown in his hands and speak the three verses over him, all at once. He listens through them with the crown finally where it belongs, and something in his face settles the rest of the way. The gray lifts from the vale by morning and does not come back. The barrow doors stand open behind you — you made the reeve no promise to shut them. By harvest the orchard rows hang heavy with fruit no one expected this year, and the vale keeps a bowl of grain on the barrow steps out of a habit nobody can quite explain.

actions.label: return the crown and speak the three verses, sealing the barrow after, as you promised the reeve
fx: You set the crown in his hands and speak the three verses over him, all at once. He listens through them with the crown finally where it belongs, and something in his face settles the rest of the way. The gray lifts from the vale by morning and does not come back. True to your word, the barrow doors seal shut behind you for good. By harvest the orchard rows hang heavy with fruit no one expected this year, and the vale keeps a bowl of grain by the sealed door out of a habit nobody can quite explain.

actions.label: kneel and become the vale's new hollow king
fx: You kneel. The crown of nothing settles on you, light as ash. The vale will have a king after all — and no dawn. No one promised to seal this place; now no one needs to.

actions.label: kneel and become the vale's new hollow king
fx: You kneel. The crown of nothing settles on you, light as ash. The vale will have a king after all — and no dawn. The seal you promised the reeve no longer matters — you are what the doors would have kept in.

topics.label: the blight
topics.say: It kills slow. Crops first, then cattle, then the will to stay. It started the night the barrow opened.

topics.label: the barrow
topics.say: Seal it. Whatever is down there, promise me you'll seal it under stone and the watch stands with you. Mind — the gray priest wants those doors opened, not shut, and won't thank you for my errand. Promise us both and you'll have promised neither.

topics.label: promise to seal the barrow
topics.say: Good. The watch stands with you now.

topics.label: the watch's aid
topics.say: Then take the watch shield. It has stopped worse than claws.

topics.label: rumors
topics.say: Verses, they say. One in the drowned shrine east of the wood, one up the old watchtower north of that, one cut into the barrow stone itself. A scholar's eye reads them quick — anyone else will have to puzzle them out slow. Some skip the puzzle and press the elder for the old king's locked crown instead. The hunter west trades herbs.

topics.label: rumors
topics.say: Verses, they say — one in the drowned shrine, one up the old watchtower, one cut into the barrow stone, slow going without a scholar's eye — there's a wandering scholar warming their hands by this very fire, if you ask them the trick of it. Word is the elder holds something taken from the old king himself; a silver tongue might settle that debt quicker than any verse. The hunter west trades herbs.

topics.label: rumors
topics.say: Verses, they say — one in the drowned shrine, one up the old watchtower, one cut into the barrow stone, slow going without a scholar's eye — there's a wandering scholar warming their hands by this very fire, if you ask them the trick of it. Quiet hands can trace the shrine's verse by touch, though, same as they find their own ways in where doors won't open — the tower and the stone still want slow going. Some skip the puzzle altogether and press the elder for the old king's locked crown instead. The hunter west trades herbs.

topics.label: rumors
topics.say: Verses, they say — one in the drowned shrine, one up the old watchtower, one cut into the barrow stone, slow going without a scholar's eye — there's a wandering scholar warming their hands by this very fire, if you ask them the trick of it. Whatever's down there, plenty would rather you just settle it with steel. Others skip the verses entirely and press the elder for the old king's locked crown instead. The hunter west trades herbs.

topics.label: ask about reading the old tongue
topics.say: You've the trick already — a scholar's eye reads these stones outright, no tip of mine needed there. Still, carry it with you: a sharper mind serves wherever else you must puzzle a way through by wits alone.

topics.label: ask about reading the old tongue
topics.say: I've spent years on stones like these. Watch how the marks repeat, and the pattern starts to show. Carry that with you — it should ease any verse you find out there.

topics.label: the old king
topics.say: He was a good king, long ago, and he was robbed in his grave. Grief like that does not lie quiet. Ask me for a blessing and I will open the barrow doors myself — no strength needed.

topics.label: the old king
topics.say: He was a good king, long ago, and he was robbed in his grave. Grief like that does not lie quiet. You have already given the reeve your word, though — I will not offer what undoes it. The doors must open some other way now.

topics.label: a blessing for the barrow
topics.say: Go with the gray blessing, then. Far off on the hill, the stone doors glow faintly and creak open — go whenever you're ready.

topics.label: ask to be released from your promise to the reeve
topics.say: Vows are not mine to unmake, only to witness broken. I'll say nothing to the reeve of it — but you will have to, in the end. Go with a clear path, if not a clear conscience.

topics.label: steel for the barrow
topics.say: Take the plain sword — and hold still, I'll put a working edge on whatever you carry.

topics.label: the vale
topics.say: Four hundred years this village has kept the wood's edge. It will not end on my page of the ledger.

topics.label: what proof he wants
topics.say: "Proof," the elder says. "His grievance, in his own words, or something bearing his mark. You have neither yet."

topics.label: what proof he wants
topics.say: "You have his seal," the elder says, "but not his grievance. Words carry more weight with me than metal."

topics.label: what proof he wants
topics.say: "You've heard his grief," the elder says. "His seal would settle it outright — but your word alone may yet be enough."

topics.label: what proof he wants
topics.say: "You have both," the elder says. "His grievance, and his seal to back it. Nothing holds this coffer shut now but my own doubt."

topics.label: the sealed coffer
topics.say: You ask about the coffer. The elder's hand covers the ledger. "That's not open to asking — not from you, not yet. Go hear what the dead king himself grieves over, up in the barrow. A token bearing his mark, if you find one there, would prove it outright — but even without one, come back and tell me what he grieves over. That may be reason enough."

topics.label: the sealed coffer
topics.say: You set the king's seal on the table between you. The elder's hand stills on the ledger — recognition, not surprise. "That mark is real. I know it." But their grip doesn't loosen. "Metal doesn't settle what's between him and me. Go hear what he grieves over yourself, up in the barrow — then come back and we'll speak of the coffer."

topics.label: the sealed coffer
topics.say: No lock holds this shut, only the elder's own doubt. You press the old king's grievance on them, your word against their will, and the elder's hands close on the ledger.
fx: Your words find the old argument the elder has been having with themself, and settle it. The coffer creaks open. The crown is old iron, heavy for its size.

topics.label: the sealed coffer
topics.say: You set the king's own seal on the ledger, his hand plain in the scrap beneath it — proof no words could match. The elder's doubt has nowhere left to stand.
fx: The coffer opens without another word. The crown is old iron, heavy for its size.

topics.label: the sealed coffer
topics.say: No lock holds this shut, only the elder's own doubt. You press the old king's grievance on them, your word against their will, and the elder's hands close on the ledger.
fx: At last your will outlasts the elder's. Their hands unclench, and they open the coffer. The crown is old iron, heavy for its size.
The elder's resolve holds, this time. Ask again, the same question, and press harder — the coffer will give eventually. Or leave it: the barrow verses reach the same end without the crown.

topics.label: the wood
topics.say: Wolves gone gray and wrong. Keep moving and keep iron close.

topics.label: trade for herbs
topics.say: Take them. Pay me by ending this.

ash_wolf.name: ash wolf
onDeath: The wolf drops. Its gray coat goes to dust.

gaunt_wolf.name: gaunt wolf
onDeath: The gaunt wolf falls still. Its ribs show plain through the gray coat.

barrow_wight.name: barrow-wight
onDeath: The wight comes apart into rag and bone.

hollow_king.name: hollow king

topics.label: why do you linger
topics.say: My crown. The first reeve took it from my barrow, and my rest went with it — the elder keeps it sealed away now. Bring it back, or speak the old verses here if you know them — either will let me rest. Finish what the thief began, or kneel and take the crown for your own — then you would linger here in my place, and no dawn would come for you.

topics.label: the blight
topics.say: It is my grief, spilled over the land. It will not stop while I wake. Ask why I linger, if you want the whole of it.

topics.label: you may soon rest
topics.say: He lifts his head, though you have spoken nothing yet. "Three," he says, quiet. "I felt each one settle into the stone as you found it. Say them here, when you're ready, and let this be over."

onDeath: Your blade finds him and he breaks apart into dust and old iron, a king who never got his crown back. The blight dies with him — the gray thins out of the trees by morning. The vale will not know why. Only that the light came back. By spring, wildflowers crowd the barrow mound, and children dare each other to touch the door that used to keep them awake at night.
